clues: Mountain forest forms a belt around the base of an isolated volcanic massif.
Large mammals inhabit the protected area around a peak that rises far above nearby plains.
Its snowy summit creates a striking contrast with the surrounding savannah.
The mountain reaches 5,895 metres, making it the highest point on the African continent.
Find Tanzania’s national park protecting the great free-standing volcanic mountain near the Kenyan border.
targetLabel: Kilimanjaro National Park — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: An isolated volcano can connect sharply different environments over a short horizontal distance. Here the source describes mountain forest, savannah surroundings and Africa’s highest summit. The park reference point represents the protected massif; it is not a claim that all of this mountain occupies one exact point.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
